name: AI / Robotics
tagline: The hottest theme — but the central question is overlap: many 'AI' funds are stuffed with NVIDIA/Micron/AMD/Alphabet you likely already own via a cheap index fund. The genuine robotics plays (ABB, Keyence, Fanuc) cost more but give differentiated exposure.
universe_note: A deep, crowded theme. Genuine ROBOTICS/AUTOMATION (BOTZ, ROBO, ROBT, THNQ) vs AI/SEMICONDUCTOR-heavy (ARTY, CHAT, AIQ, IGPT, WTAI) — the latter overlap QQQ/SMH heavily. SMH & XT are references. Use 'Add ticker' for others (ROBT peers, AIQ peers).
key_tensions: Mega-cap overlap is the #1 issue: AI funds like ARTY/CHAT lean on NVIDIA, Micron, AMD, Alphabet, Microsoft — the same names you already own in any S&P/Nasdaq fund. You may be paying a thematic fee for exposure you already have.
AI ≠ robotics: BOTZ/ROBO own industrial-automation makers (ABB, Keyence, Fanuc, Intuitive Surgical); ARTY/CHAT own chips + AI software. Very different bets under one 'AI/robotics' banner.
Cost premium vs cheap QQQ: thematic fees run 0.47-0.95% vs QQQ's 0.18%. Is the differentiated exposure worth ~3-5x the fee, given the overlap?
Concentration: ARTY/CHAT top-10 ~44-48%; even 'diversified' robotics funds lean on a few big automation names. Single-stock risk is real.
Foreign exposure: genuine robotics funds hold Japanese/European names (Keyence, Fanuc, ABB) — adds currency and geographic risk but also true diversification away from US mega-cap tech.
Fund churn: iShares DELISTED IRBO (May 2026) and repositioned it into ARTY — a reminder that even big-issuer thematic funds get reshuffled.
benchmark_note: QQQ (Nasdaq-100) is the yardstick, NOT a theme fund. At 0.18% it already gives you huge AI exposure (NVIDIA ~9%, the mega-cap AI leaders). Compare each thematic fund to QQQ: if it just owns the same mega-caps at 3-5x the fee, the theme premium isn't buying much.
